newsitem.title: UK: Med crude values slip as supply crisis eases.
newsitem.headline: Med crude values slip as supply crisis eases.

text.p: Mediterranean crude prices began to slide on Tuesday, feeling the effect of the promised resumption of Iraqi exports and the completion of Turkey's sour crude buy tender, traders said.

Outright values fell sharply on Monday on news Iraq and the U.N.had agreed details of an aid distribution plan that Baghdad wanted finalised before it resumed exports under the second term of its oil-for-food deal.

Foreign officials in Baghdad said on Tuesday they saw no major obstacles in the way of the exports, with the pricing formula unlikely to be a problem once the U.N. Secretary-General signs off on the aid plan next Monday.
Most Med crude traders predicted Iraqi barrels would reappear in early August and hoped to defer purchases until then if possible.
Oil supply in the interim before Kirkuk blend reappears has also been improved by reports that Turkey's tender for 300,000 tonnes of sour crude was filled with grades other than Russian Urals.

Although official results have not been released traders said state oil company Tupras took 130,000 and 60,000 tonne parcels of Iranian heavy, 70,000 tonnes of Syrian Light and 60,000 tonnes of Tengiz crude.

The Iranian heavy was heard priced at $1.50 below dated Brent, while the Syrian was believed accepted at 20 cents a barrel over the official selling price and no numbers were reported for the Tengiz barrels.
With the tender out of the way small parcels of Russian Urals held in reserve emerged onto the spot market.
One July 19-21 cargo was offered at 55 cents below Dated Brent, a number described as ridiculous by a rival, particularly as another cargo in the same date range was on offer at -80 cents.
"I think there is enough end-month demand to absorb what Urals is available but those who can wait will wait as there is potential for Iraq barrels in early August," said one trader.
Most players put fair value for Urals barrels at around -85/-75 cents, down some 10 cents since last week.
The imminent reappearance of Kirkuk blend at the load port of Ceyhan in Turkey has also hit term price discussions for Syrian and Algerian grades, with buyers looking askance at opening offers.

State-owned Sytrol has telexed a price of 40 cents below Dated Brent for Syrian Light in August, a 15 cent a barrel increase on July's price, said dealers, who expected to respond some time this week.
Algeria's Sonatrach reportedly asked a premium of 50 to 55 cents over dated Brent for its Saharan Blend in August, some 10 to 15 cents a barrel above values agreed for July.
One lifter said he expected the Sonatrach offer negotiated down to around 40 to 45 cents over Dated Brent.
West African markets continued steady and firm with Asian purchases down to around 11 million barrels of August loading crude from the 24 million peak buying seen in July.

A cargo of Bonny Light (second decade August) was heard traded around dated Brent +47 cents on Friday as was a Bonny Light/Medium into the Mediterranean around Dated Brent +50 cents and Dated Brent +17-21 cents respectively.
Forcados was assessed around Dated +28-30 cents with Qua Iboe around Dated +38-40 cents.
